notes: US name 'motorola razr - 2026' and global name 'motorola razr 70' are ONE physical device, stated by Motorola itself: the April 29, 2026 press release's availability section pairs 'the new motorola razr – 2026' (United States) with 'motorola razr 70 ... in Europe, Middle East, Africa, and Latin America'. Corroborated by identical published geometry on both product pages (88.08 x 73.99 x 15.85 closed, 171.30 x 73.99 x 7.25 open, 188 g) and near-identical product codes (pmipmjl44m7 US / pmipmjl44m6 GB). Motorola's 2026 pages label the triples explicitly 'Dimensions (H x W x D) (Closed)/(Open)', so the mapping is the manufacturer's own. Resolutions recorded [width, height] exactly as Motorola prints them ('1080 x 2640', '1056 x 1066'); Motorola states no orientation for the near-square cover panel. Aspect taken from the GB page ('22:9'); the US page prints '22:09'. Panel recorded as OLED - Motorola's words are 'LTPO Extreme AMOLED' (main) and 'LTPS Extreme AMOLED' (cover). announced/released read from Motorola's own press release via a web.archive.org snapshot dated 2026-05-21, because motorolanews.com returns HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and curl; May 21 is the US on-sale date. hinge.crease null - Motorola never states a crease shape. Motorola also states this model meets MIL-STD 810H and IP48, and calls it 'the first flip smartphone in the category that meets military standards for durability' - no field exists for that here. || EVIDENCE SWEEP 2026-09-13: these values were present in the research pass but carried NO sources[] entry covering their field, so they were set to null per the registry rule (a value without a citation is an assertion, not evidence). Preserved verbatim here so a human can re-source rather than re-research: hinge.type = 'flip'; hinge.axis = 'short'.
